graduation.title: 2026 graduation projects exhibition
graduation.description: The faculty hosted its annual graduation projects exhibition with more than 40 projects in artificial intelligence and data science.
graduation.content:
The faculty held its annual graduation projects exhibition for the class of 2026. Students, faculty members, and guest reviewers attended.

More than 40 projects were shown in artificial intelligence, data science, web and mobile development, the Internet of Things, software engineering, data analytics, and cybersecurity.

Teams presented their work to a review panel and answered questions on design, implementation, and next steps. Judges noted strong technical work in several projects and gave feedback on scalability, security, and usability.

The faculty said the exhibition lets students present work from their studies in a public setting. Several teams received recognition at the closing session.

aiWorkshop.title: Applied AI workshop series starts
aiWorkshop.description: The faculty is running a workshop series on applied artificial intelligence with industry guests.
aiWorkshop.content:
The faculty started a workshop series on applied artificial intelligence with guest instructors from industry.

Sessions cover machine learning basics, data preparation, model building, and evaluation. Students work on small exercises using current tools.

Topics include classification, prediction, natural language processing, and computer vision. The series also outlines common job paths in AI and data work.

More workshops on related subjects are planned later in the year.

partnership.title: Faculty signs tech partnership agreement
partnership.description: A cooperation agreement covers student training, hiring paths, and curriculum input from partner companies.
partnership.content:
The faculty signed a cooperation agreement with technology companies covering student training, hiring, and curriculum review.

Students may train with partner firms during semesters and breaks. Company staff will also give talks on programming, AI, data science, cybersecurity, and cloud computing.

Industry input will help update course content. Students and staff may join applied projects linked to company needs.

The faculty said the agreement should expand training and employment options for students and graduates.

studentCompetition.title: Students place well in programming contest
studentCompetition.description: A faculty team competed against students from several Egyptian universities.
studentCompetition.content:
A faculty student team took part in a programming contest with teams from other Egyptian universities. Each team had limited time to solve a set of problems.

The team trained on algorithms, data structures, and timed problem solving before the event. During the contest they solved several difficult problems and placed well.

Members said the event helped them test skills from their coursework under competition conditions. The faculty encourages more students to join programming contests and offers training sessions.

dataScienceConference.title: Data science conference at the faculty
dataScienceConference.description: Researchers and professionals met to discuss recent work in data science and AI.
dataScienceConference.content:
The faculty held a conference on data science and artificial intelligence with researchers, staff, and industry speakers.

Talks covered big data, machine learning, data visualization, and data quality. Discussion sessions addressed privacy, security, and data management in organizations.

Students asked questions about tools used in industry and career options after graduation. Examples from healthcare, education, business, and government were presented.

The faculty said it will continue similar events during the year.

technologyAgreement.title: New student innovation initiative
technologyAgreement.description: The faculty announced support for students with technical project ideas and early startup work.
technologyAgreement.content:
The faculty opened a program to help students turn technical ideas into working projects.

Workshops cover entrepreneurship, project management, market research, and basic business planning. Students can pitch ideas to reviewers and receive feedback.

The faculty asks teams to mix programming, design, data, and business skills where possible. Information on incubators, competitions, and funding sources is also provided.

Further sessions for student founders are planned.
